title: K-flat tensor with a degree-zero module on a ringed site
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a site essentially small in a coefficient universe $w$ [def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with values in $w$. Use sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their cochain complexes [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and the localization $Q_R$ to their unbounded derived category $D(R)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Give $D(R)$ the K-flat derived tensor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], for the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Let $P$ be any K-flat cochain complex [def-pc-kflat-complex], and let $M$ be any sheaf of $R$-modules. Write $M[0]$ for its complex concentrated in degree zero and define the termwise tensor complex $T_M(P)$ by
$$T_M(P)^q=P^q\otimes_R M,\qquad d_{T_M(P)}^q=d_P^q\otimes1_M.$$
There is a canonical isomorphism
$$c_{P,M}:Q_R(P)\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q_R(M[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_R(T_M(P)).$$
It is natural in chain maps between K-flat complexes and in module-sheaf maps: for $u:P\to P'$ and $f:M\to M'$, its naturality square has right-hand map $Q_R(T(u,f))$, where $T(u,f)^q=u^q\otimes f$. The comparison is the one induced by the K-flat resolution construction and the degree-zero total-tensor identification, and is independent of auxiliary resolutions. Neither boundedness nor flatness of the individual terms of $P$, nor flatness of $M$, is required.

proof.text: Construct a functorial flat-term K-flat replacement F on unbounded complexes with a natural quasi-isomorphism π:F→id. Use the reduced LeftResolution of the categorical flat subcategory, its resolutionFunctor and resolutionNatTrans, and exact integer-indexed colimits of module sheaves. Its terms are flat by the flat colimit theorem, transported through siteSheafTensorRightIso. Its categorical K-flatness implies the acyclic-tensor convention by applying tensor to 0→Z for acyclic Z. Closedness and functorial flat covers are the existing independent-coefficient constructions.

source.place: Tags 06YS and 06YU; functorial flat resolutions and unbounded K-flat replacement

proof.text: The given K-flat predicate implies that tensoring in the second variable preserves quasi-isomorphisms by lem-pur-kflat-tensor-quasiiso-independent. The existing Koszul braiding of cochain complexes transports this assertion to tensoring in the first variable. Thus Tot(π_P,π_Y) is a quasi-isomorphism whenever P is K-flat: first tensor π_P with F(Y), then tensor π_Y with P.

source.place: Tags 06YN and 06YP; K-flat preservation and signed symmetry

proof.text: Let U(P,Y)=T(QP,QY) for the published site tensor and V(P,Y)=Q Tot(P,Y). The published representativeIso on flat-term K-flat pairs is natural: the left and right natural comparison functors of lem-weil-pbc-kflat-fixed-tensor-triangulated agree with representativeIso on these pairs, so compose their naturality squares. It gives b:V(F-,F-)≅U(F-,F-). The natural augmentation gives an invertible ε:U(F-,F-)→U. Define m=ε⁻¹ followed by b⁻¹ followed by V(π,π). This is natural on all complex pairs and invertible when P is K-flat by the previous step. Naturality of representativeIso for (π_A,π_B), with A,B flat-term K-flat, proves m(A,B)=representativeIso(A,B)⁻¹.

source.place: Tag 06YU; the natural comparison with flat-term K-flat representatives

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism m(P,M[0]) with Q of mapBifunctorSingle₂Iso to define c(P,M). The single-total comparison is natural simultaneously in P and M: conjugate the square by its inverses and check in degree q on the unique summand (q,0), where the induced map is u^q tensor f. Naturality of m and this chain comparison give exactly the displayed naturality equation.

source.place: Tag 06YU; degree-zero specialization of total tensor

proof.text: Naturality of m for arbitrary p:A→P and b:B→M[0], together with m(A,B)=representativeIso(A,B)⁻¹, gives the stated normalization equation (even before assuming p,b are quasi-isomorphisms). For uniqueness take A=F(P), B=F(M[0]), p=π_P and b=π_M[0]. The representative comparison and T(Qp,Qb) are invertible; cancel their composite in the two normalization equations, and use function and isomorphism extensionality. This proves independence of all auxiliary choices without boundedness or termwise-flatness assumptions on P.
